overview: Michael Hill is a specialty jewellery retailer founded in Whangarei, New Zealand in 1979 by Sir Michael Hill, now operating a simplified two-brand portfolio (Michael Hill and Bevilles) across 281 stores and ecommerce sites in Australia (157 stores, including 36 Bevilles), New Zealand (43) and Canada (81), with the legacy TenSevenSeven and Medley brands wound down during FY2026 (a non-cash write-off of $6.1m). The Group moved its primary listing to the ASX in 2016 and maintains a secondary listing on the NZX (dual-listed, quoted in NZD on NZX / AUD on ASX), designs and manufactures via its own operations, and reports its financial statements in AUD on a 52/53-week fiscal year ending in late June/early July (FY2026: 52 weeks to 28 June 2026). It is a micro-cap (~384.8m shares on issue, ASX closing price AUD 0.33 at FY26 year-end vs AUD 0.42 a year earlier) with founding director Emma Hill the largest single shareholder (167,487,526 shares, ~43.5% of shares on issue) following the July 2025 passing of founder Sir Michael Hill.

business_model.summary: Michael Hill designs, manufactures and retails jewellery, watches and related services through company-operated stores and digital channels across Australia, New Zealand and Canada. Revenue is overwhelmingly transactional (single jewellery purchases spanning bridal, gifting and self-purchase), supplemented by a genuinely material recurring/deferred-revenue stream from Professional Care Plans (PCP) -- extended-care/warranty contracts sold alongside jewellery, offered as 3-year, 10-year and lifetime plans. The FY2026 Annual Report discloses, for the first time in the filings reviewed, the actual scale of this program: a deferred PCP revenue liability of $57m at 28 June 2026, with $27m of PCP revenue recognised in the FY26 income statement -- a material ~4% of group revenue that management flags as a 'key lever' in its services-led growth engine, though revenue recognition timing (based on estimated future service usage over the life of the plan) introduces real accounting judgement (flagged as a Key Audit Matter by EY) and period-to-period volatility (H2 FY26 comparable EBIT was depressed by $4.6m of lower PCP revenue release versus H2 FY25, driven by updated repair-pattern and cost-indexation assumptions, even as the underlying in-year value of PCP plans sold grew 1.2%). FY2026 marked a genuine inflection: record group revenue of $655.7m (+1.9% reported / +4.1% constant currency), same-store sales growth of +5.2% (constant currency) across all three geographies, Comparable EBIT (a non-IFRS, unaudited normalised measure) up 57% to $24.0m (3.7% margin, from 2.4% in FY25), statutory reported EBIT up to $31.1m (from $18.9m) with the gap to Comparable EBIT explained mainly by AASB16 lease accounting add-backs, statutory NPAT up 376% to $10.0m, and the return of a dividend (AU2.0 cents per share, final, partly franked/imputed) after two dividend-free years.

business_model.customer_type: B2C mass/mid-market specialty jewellery consumer; bridal, gifting and self-purchase segments; no single customer accounts for more than 10% of consolidated revenue; Brilliance loyalty programme grew to 3.3m members in FY26, with gross profit dollars from Brilliance members up 14%
business_model.geographic_mix: FY2026 group revenue $655.7m translated as Australia $371.8m (56.7%, incl. Bevilles), Canada $186.3m (28.4%, CA$174.2m in local currency), New Zealand $97.1m (14.8%, NZ$112.4m in local currency). Local-currency segment revenue growth: Australia +2.5%, Canada +7.3%, New Zealand +3.1%. Store count 281 at FY26 year-end (Australia 157 incl. 36 Bevilles, Canada 81, New Zealand 43), down a net 6 stores from 287 a year earlier as TenSevenSeven and Medley were wound down/absorbed and the network was selectively rationalised (Australia -3, Canada -1, NZ -2).

competitive_position.market_position: Mid-market/'accessible modern luxury' positioning ('making modern luxury accessible' is the company's stated purpose) in a fragmented industry; per IBISWorld, Prouds The Jewellers holds more Australian watch-and-jewellery-retailing market share than Michael Hill, with Richemont Australia also a larger competitor by some measures. Bevilles (positioned explicitly as 'The Look For Less' -- win on value, move fast, run lean) competes at the value end against Prouds and department-store/mass jewellery counters and returned to same-store sales growth (+5.8% in H2 FY26, from -4.6% in H1) after a reset period. Canada is explicitly framed by management as the clearest growth engine with a target footprint of 85-90 stores (currently 81) given materially lower brand penetration than AU/NZ; it delivered a record FY26 (same-store sales +7.0%, online +22%, comparable EBIT +16.3% to CA$21.9m at a 12.6% margin, the Group's highest-margin segment). New Zealand is the most mature market but only returned to consistent positive same-store sales momentum through H2 FY26 (accelerating to +5.6% in H2 from a softer H1) after a prior-year -5.0% decline; NZ's comparable EBIT margin (12.5%) still exceeds Australia's (9.8%) despite slower growth, reflecting brand maturity.

moat_factors.description: In-house design and manufacturing/wholesale operations let the company control product economics and react to metal price volatility rather than relying solely on third-party vendors; gross margin was held flat at 60.5% through FY26 (Australia actually improved 130bps to 60.7%) despite gold trading at multiple record highs, evidencing genuine pricing power and product-mix agility.

281 stores across three countries function as fulfilment nodes and showrooms (Buy Online Pickup In-Store is an explicit FY27 investment priority), a structural advantage versus pure online/lab-grown-diamond disruptors that lack a trial/fitting experience for bridal purchases. Digital is now 8.7% of group revenue and the largest single 'store' in the Michael Hill brand, but management frames it as complementary rather than cannibalising.

Brilliance loyalty membership grew to 3.3m in FY26 with gross profit dollars from members up 14%. PCP (deferred revenue liability $57m, $27m recognised in FY26), a digitised Michael Hill Diamond Warranty, a re-launched bespoke jewellery offering (now in 40+ stores) and 311,857 repairs/services completed in FY26 (including a 210%+ increase in repairs of non-Michael Hill jewellery via the Re:Store program) create repeat store visits and incremental high-margin revenue beyond the initial jewellery sale.

46+-year-old brand founded by the late Sir Michael Hill (d. 29 July 2025); high brand awareness in New Zealand and Australia, less so in Canada where brand-building (increased marketing investment for FY27) remains a stated multi-year priority. "Made For You" personalised/custom orders now represent 15% of Michael Hill sales.

Mid-sized (~$656m revenue) relative to global players like Pandora and Signet Jewelers (whose former Chief Merchandising Officer, Tonia Zehrer, joined Michael Hill as Chief Product Officer in January 2026); scale is a disadvantage versus Pandora's global sourcing but an advantage versus small independents.

weaknesses: Structurally thinner competitive moat than franchise/network-effect businesses -- jewellery is a commoditised, price-comparable, big-ticket discretionary purchase, and management itself frames FY26 as still 'early stages of our business reset'

Bevilles required a $7.4m non-cash brand-intangible impairment in FY25 after a period of 'strategic drift'; the brand intangible ($11.9m carrying value at FY26 year-end) remains subject to ongoing impairment testing (flagged as a Key Audit Matter) and only returned to same-store sales growth in H2 FY26 (from -4.6% to +5.8%), so the multi-year turnaround, while now showing traction, is not yet proven over a full cycle

Statutory/Comparable EBIT margin, even after FY26's improvement, is only 3.7% (Comparable) / 4.7% (statutory EBIT-to-sales) -- far below management's own medium-term 10% ambition -- underscoring how much execution is still required; Australia (9.8%) and Canada (12.6%) run well ahead of the group average while Bevilles drags the Australian blended figure down

No commodity (gold/silver) hedging identified in the FY26 financial risk management note -- the Group's Treasury Policy explicitly covers foreign exchange (forward contracts), interest rate and credit/liquidity risk but the disclosed derivative program is FX-only (buying USD/EUR forward for inventory purchases); margin protection against precious-metal inflation relies entirely on pricing/product-mix agility, not financial hedges

Leadership and governance churn: CEO Daniel Bracken's sudden death (Feb 2025), founder Sir Michael Hill's passing (29 Jul 2025), a new CFO (Elodie Guillaumond, Feb 2026) and Company Secretary (three changes within about 16 months) and now long-serving Chair Rob Fyfe's retirement (effective 28 November 2026, succeeded by Claudia Batten) -- a run of major board/executive transitions inside roughly two years, even though each has been managed in an orderly fashion, with the Board explicitly stating it is 'refreshing skills and capability across both the executive team and the board, with succession planning a key focus'

growth_drivers: CEO Jonathan Waecker's (started August 2025) 'operational reset' -- simplified pricing/promotional architecture, tighter product focus, data-driven decision-making -- delivered a full-year proof point in FY26: Comparable EBIT up 57% to $24.0m (68% on a constant currency basis), statutory NPAT up 376% to $10.0m, record group revenue, and same-store sales growth across all three segments

Canada is the clearest structural growth engine: record FY26 (same-store sales +7.0%, online +22%, comparable EBIT +16.3% to CA$21.9m at a 12.6% margin -- the Group's best), with a stated footprint target of 85-90 stores (from 81) and FY27 plans to modernise five of its top six stores across Toronto, Vancouver, Calgary and Edmonton

Brand portfolio simplified from 5 brands to 2 (Michael Hill + Bevilles) during FY26 -- TenSevenSeven and Medley wound down (a $6.1m non-cash write-off, excluded from Comparable EBIT) -- freeing capital and management attention for the two brands with the clearest value proposition

Bevilles 'Reset, Perform, Grow' turnaround delivered its first positive half in H2 FY26 (same-store sales +5.8% from -4.6% in H1; gross margin up 660bps H2-on-H1), setting up a potential re-expansion decision once further gates are cleared

Digital/omni-channel growth continues to outpace total sales growth (Michael Hill brand online +10% constant currency, Canada +22%), with management stating digital penetration (8.7% of group revenue) remains 'below that of many comparable peers' and sizing significant further runway; FY27 priorities include expanded Buy Online Pickup In-Store and enhanced clienteling tools

Balance sheet transformation: net debt fell from $41.9m (FY25) to $5.5m (FY26), a $36.3m improvement, driven by disciplined inventory management (-$9.4m, GMROI productivity +13%), stronger cash generation, a one-off $7.5m Australian income tax refund in H2, continued cost discipline and improved supplier terms -- plus the debt facility was refinanced for two more years with ANZ and a new lender, CBA, was added

Return of the dividend: a final FY26 dividend of AU2.0 cents/share (50% franked for Australian purposes, 50% imputed for NZ purposes, with conduit foreign income) was declared, ending a two-year suspension; franking credits of $9.2m and NZ imputation credits of NZ$6.5m remain available to support future distributions

Management's medium-term ambition of a 10% group EBIT margin (from FY26's 3.7% Comparable EBIT margin, up from 2.4% in FY25) via four explicit levers -- improved store productivity, diversified revenue growth, gross profit/margin improvement, and operating leverage (cost of doing business improved 70bps to 57.1% of revenue in FY26) -- first articulated at the 14 April 2026 Investor Day and reaffirmed with FY26 results

Early FY27 trading (first 8 weeks) showed continued momentum: group same-store sales +4.4% constant currency (Canada +9.8%, New Zealand +3.3%, Australia +1.7%), with gross margins also strengthening year-on-year, suggesting the reset has legs beyond a single strong year

AI-driven productivity initiatives: a partnership with Impact Analytics for AI-based demand forecasting/inventory planning, and the in-house 'Retail Assist' tool now handling more than 50% of retail support enquiries, are explicit levers for FY27 operating leverage and inventory efficiency

Stated Michael Hill brand ambition to grow revenue 'beyond $700M' (from the current ~$656m Group total, of which Michael Hill Australia+NZ+Canada is the large majority) as part of the 'Grow Customers, Grow Profit, Grow Engagement' strategic framework

business.risk: Gold and silver input cost inflation
business.description: Gold has traded at repeated record highs, described by the outgoing Chair as 'the near doubling of the gold price over the past two years.' Management held gross margin at 60.5% in both FY25 and FY26 only via disciplined pricing execution and product/mix management -- the FY26 financial risk management note confirms there is no financial hedging program for gold/precious metals (only FX forward contracts for currency exposure), so margin protection is entirely a pricing/execution outcome that could fail if gold volatility outpaces the company's ability to reprice or if promotional intensity increases in a soft consumer environment.

The Bevilles brand intangible ($11.9m carrying value) took a $7.4m non-cash impairment in FY25 and remains an EY Key Audit Matter given the judgement involved in impairment testing (relief-from-royalty method, cash flow forecasts, discount rate); H2 FY26 was the first period of demonstrated recovery (same-store sales +5.8% from -4.6%, gross margin +660bps) after a multi-year reset -- one strong half is encouraging but not yet a full-cycle proof point.

business.risk: PCP (Professional Care Plan) revenue recognition volatility
business.description: The FY26 Annual Report discloses a $57m deferred PCP revenue liability and $27m of PCP revenue recognised in FY26 -- a material and previously undisclosed revenue stream. Recognition depends on management's estimate of actual services used relative to expected services over lifetime, 10-year and 3-year plans; assumptions (repair patterns, cost indexation) are reviewed annually and cumulative catch-up adjustments can swing reported profit -- H2 FY26 comparable EBIT absorbed a $4.6m headwind purely from lower PCP revenue release versus H2 FY25, even though underlying in-year PCP plan sales grew 1.2%. EY has flagged this as a Key Audit Matter given the estimation judgement involved.

business.risk: Structural competitive/margin pressure from lab-grown diamonds
business.description: The Group's own Directors' Report risk table explicitly names 'competition between mined and laboratory created diamonds, vendor consolidation and changing market perceptions' as a top risk that 'may impact pricing of our range and could influence consumer behaviours to the detriment of one or both precious stones.' Lab-grown diamond wholesale prices have fallen sharply since 2018-2020 industry-wide as global production capacity surged; MHJ's stated mitigant is that both mined and lab-grown diamonds feature in its core range (with FY27 product strategy explicitly 'capturing the full diamond opportunity: premium lab-grown diamonds capture growth, natural diamonds reinforce premium positioning').

Long-serving Chair Rob Fyfe (director since 2016, Chair since June 2021) is retiring effective 28 November 2026, succeeded by current Deputy Chair/non-executive director Claudia Batten -- the company's own Directors' Report states it is 'refreshing skills and capability across both the Executive team and the Board, with succession planning a key focus.' This follows CEO Bracken's sudden death (Feb 2025), founder Sir Michael Hill's passing (Jul 2025), a new CFO (Feb 2026) and three Company Secretary changes within about 16 months -- a high rate of transition, even though each has been handled in an orderly, planned manner.

NZ segment revenue fell -5.0% in FY25 before recovering through FY26 to +3.1% (local currency) / same-store sales +3.6%; NZ's comparable EBIT margin (12.5%) is still the highest of the three segments (ahead of Australia's 9.8%), so the risk is one of a low ceiling on growth in a mature, brand-saturated market rather than an ongoing decline.

The Directors' Report explicitly flags rising theft/violence risk during periods of financial hardship (an executive-led taskforce is in place) and increasing cyber-attack risk given reliance on third-party platforms, overseen by a Technology Governance Committee; the rapid adoption of AI across the business is separately flagged as introducing governance, data management and benefits-realisation risk if not appropriately controlled.

financial.risk: Dividend resumption is recent and modest
financial.description: No interim or final dividend was paid for FY2024 (final) or FY2025; a final FY2026 dividend of AU2.0 cents/share (50% franked/50% imputed) was declared in August 2026 (dividend cover 1.30x by NPAT), ending the two-year suspension -- but it is a single small payment on a still-thin earnings base ($10.0m statutory NPAT) and a renewed downturn could see it paused again.

financial.risk: Net debt / seasonal working capital reliance
financial.description: Net debt fell sharply from $41.9m (FY25) to $5.5m (FY26), a $36.3m improvement, driven substantially by inventory reduction (-$9.4m, GMROI productivity +13%), a one-off $7.5m Australian tax refund, and the debt facility refinanced for two more years with ANZ, adding CBA as a new lender (net borrowings to equity fell to 3.2% from 24.5%) -- a significant de-risking event, though the business still has historically negative seasonal working-capital swings around Christmas trading, against which management notes 'significant headroom' remains.

FY26 effective tax rate was an unusually high 43.5% (FY25: 4.3%; FY24: 30.2%), reflecting one-off items including the Australian tax refund; investors should not extrapolate either FY25's near-zero rate or FY26's elevated rate as a normalised run-rate.

FY27 capital expenditure and SaaS implementation costs are guided to increase to approximately $25m (from $19.7m in FY26, which was itself in line with FY25's $19.7m-equivalent spend, comprising $12.5m property/fit-out, $5.9m SaaS and $1.3m intangibles), funding further store refreshes and AI-driven inventory/merchandising tools -- a moderate step-up in cash outflow management expects to fund from the now much-stronger balance sheet, but it will pressure free cash flow if same-store sales momentum stalls.

regulatory.risk: Consumer protection / extended warranty (PCP) compliance history
regulatory.description: Michael Hill was fined NZ$169,000 by the NZ Commerce Commission in 2018 for Professional Care Plan (extended warranty) disclosure failures. With the FY26 Annual Report now disclosing a $57m PCP deferred revenue liability and $27m of annual PCP revenue, this establishes PCP as a materially larger and more scrutinised revenue line than previously visible, in jurisdictions with active consumer-protection regulators.

The Group published its first mandatory climate-related disclosure report in FY26 under the Australian Sustainability Reporting Standard AASB S2, incurring new compliance cost (regulatory sustainability report assurance fees of $30,000 paid to EY in FY26, on top of $676,636 in statutory audit fees). It separately relies on the NZ Financial Markets Conduct (Climate-related Disclosures for Overseas Climate Reporting Entities) Exemption Notice 2026 to avoid duplicative NZ climate reporting, given its ASX primary listing (reconfirmed 22 September 2026 for the FY26 period).
Standard multinational retailer risk relating to transfer pricing policy across AU/NZ/Canada operations, explicitly named in the Group's own forward-looking-statement risk factors.

macro.description: Jewellery is a highly discretionary, big-ticket purchase category. The outgoing Chair's letter explicitly cites 'cost-of-living pressures,' variable interest rates, currency movements and commodity prices, and 'ongoing conflict and geopolitical tension' adding 'further uncertainty to energy costs, inflation and consumer sentiment' -- the strength of the FY26 recovery has not yet been tested by a genuine consumer downturn.

macro.risk: Gold and precious metal price volatility
macro.description: Record gold and silver prices persisted through FY25 and FY26 (gold described as having 'nearly doubled' over two years) as the single largest identified cost pressure; further increases would test the company's ability to reprice without demand destruction, particularly in a still-promotional retail environment, given the absence of a financial hedging program for the commodity.

Reports in AUD but generates meaningful revenue in NZD and CAD; a 10% AUD appreciation would reduce FY26 pre-tax profit by an estimated $0.67m per the disclosed FX sensitivity analysis (a 10% AUD depreciation would increase it by $0.82m), and FX moves explain the gap between reported (+1.9%) and constant-currency (+4.1%) group revenue growth even when local-currency segment performance is stable or improving. The Group does not hedge its intercompany loan FX exposure.

Direct effect via net debt/facility interest cost is now much reduced given the swing to near-net-cash ($5.5m net debt at FY26 year-end, interest cover improved to 2.3x from 1.1x); the Group is exposed to interest rate risk principally through cash balances and variable-rate borrowings, with interest rate swaps identified as an available (though not confirmed as currently used) management tool. Indirect effect via mortgage-rate-driven household discretionary spending capacity in Australia, NZ and Canada remains relevant.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Australian and comparable jewellery markets are low-growth/mature and fragmented; industry-wide pressure from lab-grown diamond price deflation is reshaping category economics even as unit demand for lab-grown stones grows sharply, a dynamic MHJ's own Directors' Report names as a principal risk to manage rather than avoid
macro_factors.cyclicality: High -- jewellery (particularly non-bridal, gifting and self-purchase categories) is one of the more cyclical/discretionary retail categories, sensitive to consumer confidence, employment and interest-rate-driven household budgets; bridal demand is comparatively more resilient (a 'life milestone' purchase, and Canada's bridal growth specifically is highlighted as attracting higher-lifetime-value customers), which management explicitly leans into as a stabilising segment
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-to-moderate direct impact via net debt funding cost (now minimal given the near-net-cash position and 2.3x interest cover) and material indirect impact via consumer discretionary spending capacity across all three operating geographies

recent_developments.event: Jonathan Waecker (previously Chief Customer & Sales Officer, The Warehouse Group; prior roles at Disney and Yahoo) commenced as CEO, succeeding interim CEO Andrew Lowe (CFO), following the sudden death of CEO Daniel Bracken (Feb 2025).

H1 FY2026 results (26 weeks to 28 Dec 2025): revenue $370.95m (up 3.0%), EBIT $38.9m (up 20.1%), NPAT $22.3m (up 32.0%); group same-store sales +3.8%. No interim dividend declared, but Board signalled intent to resume at the FY26 full-year result. Debt facility refinanced for two more years with ANZ, adding CBA as a new lender.

Elodie Guillaumond stepped into the CFO role (formally appointed February 2026), succeeding Andrew Lowe, who departed the business on 17 February 2026 after returning to his substantive CFO role following his period as interim CEO.

ACC (New Zealand's state accident insurer) built a substantial shareholding, disclosing 2.48% on 31 March 2026 and increasing to 5.819% (22,393,710 shares) via ASX market purchases by 10 April 2026 -- an institutional accumulation signal.

Investor Day in Brisbane: CEO detailed the operational reset framework, brand simplification from 5 to 2 brands (Michael Hill + Bevilles; TenSevenSeven and Medley wound down by end of FY26), a medium-term ambition of a 10% group EBIT margin, and confirmed intent to return to dividends at the FY26 full-year result.
Tonia Zehrer, former Senior Vice President and Chief Merchandising Officer at Signet Jewelers (the world's largest diamond jewellery retailer), joined as Chief Product Officer in January 2026.
FY2026 trading update ahead of full results: group sales up ~2.0% reported / +3.9% constant currency; same-store sales +3% reported / +5.2% constant currency; comparable EBIT guided to $22-24m.

FY2026 full-year results (52 weeks to 28 June 2026): record group revenue $655.7m (+1.9% reported, +4.1% constant currency); same-store sales +5.2% (constant currency) across all three markets (Canada +7.0%, Australia +4.8%, New Zealand +3.6%); Comparable EBIT up 57% to $24.0m (3.7% margin, from 2.4% FY25; +68% on constant currency); statutory reported EBIT $31.1m (from $18.9m); statutory NPAT up 376% to $10.0m; gross margin held flat at 60.5%; net debt cut from $41.9m to $5.5m; inventory down $9.4m to $189.7m with GMROI productivity up 13%; PCP deferred revenue liability disclosed at $57m ($27m recognised as revenue in FY26). Board declared a final dividend of AU2.0 cents/share (50% franked/50% imputed) -- the first dividend since FY2023/24.

Board announcement: Chair Rob Fyfe (director since 2016, chair since June 2021) will retire effective 28 November 2026; Deputy Chair and current non-executive director Claudia Batten will succeed him. Company flagged a broader refresh of skills/capability across the executive team and board, with succession planning a stated focus. Marketing chief Jo Feeney also left the Group in August 2026.

Company confirmed it again qualifies for New Zealand's climate-related disclosure exemption for overseas reporting entities for the FY26 accounting period, relying on its ASX primary listing and its own separately lodged AASB S2 Sustainability Report.

Management disclosed the first eight weeks of FY2027 trading showed group same-store sales +4.4% constant currency (Canada +9.8%, New Zealand +3.3%, Australia +1.7%), flat in AUD, with gross margins strengthening year-on-year despite an uncertain macro backdrop; management expects 'continued profitable growth through the year.'

items.notes: CFO Elodie Guillaumond guided gross margin to be held or nominally improved, continuing the FY25-FY26 pattern of defending margin through pricing/mix discipline despite elevated precious-metal costs.

items.notes: Framed under the 'Grow Customers' pillar of the 'Making Modern Luxury Accessible' strategy for the Michael Hill brand specifically (group total revenue was $655.7m in FY26, of which Michael Hill brand is the large majority alongside Bevilles).

items.notes: Disclosed alongside FY26 results as an early read, with segment detail: Canada +9.8%, New Zealand +3.3%, Australia +1.7% (local currency). Gross margins also reported as strengthening year-on-year early in FY27.

items.notes: Dividend cover of 1.30x by NPAT for the amount declared relating to the year. Chair Fyfe framed the resumption as reflecting 'a materially stronger balance sheet and improved operating performance,' with continuity into early FY27 trading, while stressing continued capital discipline.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Jonathan Waecker: the reset built around excellent retail fundamentals -- listening to customers and people, sharpening product curation, price architecture and promotional discipline -- delivered 'a strong turnaround in FY26, with record Group revenue, comparable EBIT up 57%, and the restoration of dividends,' while stressing 'we're not even a full year into this reset, and there's plenty more to do.' Strategic framing has shifted to 'making modern luxury accessible' for Michael Hill (three pillars: grow customers, grow profit, grow engagement) and 'The Look For Less' for Bevilles (win on value, move fast, run lean). CFO Elodie Guillaumond guided FY27 gross margin flat-to-up and CODB flat-to-down, consistent with the operating-leverage path to the 10% medium-term EBIT margin ambition. Outgoing Chair Rob Fyfe's retirement (effective 28 Nov 2026) was framed as a natural handover point now that the turnaround has stabilised, explicitly citing his original intention to leave in mid-2025 delayed to 'support continuity, oversee the appointment of our new Chief Executive Officer and help prepare the Company for its next chapter'; incoming Chair Claudia Batten inherits a considerably de-risked balance sheet and a company explicitly refreshing board/executive skills and succession planning.

bull_case: FY2026 delivered a genuine, broad-based inflection rather than a one-off: Comparable EBIT up 57% to $24.0m, statutory NPAT up 376% to $10.0m, record group revenue, and same-store sales growth in all three segments (including New Zealand and Bevilles, the two prior laggards) -- with early FY27 trading (+4.4% constant-currency same-store sales in the first 8 weeks) suggesting the momentum is continuing, not fading

Balance sheet has been transformed: net debt cut from $41.9m to $5.5m in a single year, inventory down $9.4m with GMROI productivity up 13%, interest cover improved to 2.3x from 1.1x, and the debt facility refinanced on improved terms with an added lender (CBA) -- creating real capacity for reinvestment (FY27 capex/SaaS up to ~$25m) and dividends without balance-sheet strain

Dividend resumed (AU2.0 cents/share final FY26, partly franked/imputed, 1.30x covered) after a two-year suspension, re-establishing an income-support underpin for the stock and signalling Board confidence, with $9.2m of franking credits and NZ$6.5m of imputation credits available to support future distributions

Canada is a genuine, underpenetrated growth market delivering a record year (same-store sales +7.0%, online +22%, best-in-group 12.6% comparable EBIT margin) with a credible medium-term store-count expansion plan (85-90 stores from 81) and lower brand penetration than the mature AU/NZ markets, giving a long multi-year runway

Gross margin has proven durably resilient (60.5%, and actually improved 130bps in Australia to 60.7%) through a record gold/silver price cycle via pricing/mix discipline, evidencing genuine pricing power; management's 10% medium-term EBIT margin ambition (from 3.7% Comparable achieved in FY26) still implies substantial further re-rating upside if even partially delivered, with the newly-disclosed $57m PCP deferred-revenue liability representing a further embedded, high-margin earnings stream still working through the P&L
bear_case: The FY26 turnaround, while real, is a single strong year off a very depressed base (FY25 Comparable EBIT margin was just 2.4%); a 3.7% margin (4.7% statutory EBIT-to-sales) is still far from the 10% medium-term ambition, and the market may already be pricing in continued flawless execution that has not yet been tested through a full economic cycle or a genuine consumer downturn -- the company's own Chair's letter describes the business as still at 'the early stages of our business reset'

Record and potentially still-rising gold and silver prices remain a persistent structural cost headwind for a jewellery retailer with a confirmed absence of any financial hedging program for precious metals (the Group's disclosed derivative use is FX-only); margin protection depends entirely on repricing/product-mix execution, which is a fragile buffer if the consumer discretionary backdrop weakens or promotional intensity rises industry-wide

PCP revenue recognition ($57m deferred liability, $27m recognised in FY26) is a Key Audit Matter subject to significant management judgement and assumption changes -- H2 FY26 comparable EBIT already absorbed a $4.6m headwind purely from revised PCP assumptions, illustrating that a meaningful slice of reported profit is an accounting estimate that can move independently of underlying trading

Governance continuity risk: long-serving Chair Rob Fyfe is retiring (effective Nov 2026) just as the company explicitly signals a broader 'refresh' of board and executive skills/succession planning -- on top of the CEO's sudden death (2025), the founder's passing (2025), a new CFO (2026) and three Company Secretary changes in ~16 months, this is a high cadence of leadership transition, even though each has so far been managed in an orderly way

Bevilles' recovery (positive same-store sales only from H2 FY26, brand intangible still carried at $11.9m and subject to ongoing impairment-testing judgement) and New Zealand's stabilisation are each less than a full year old; both remain unproven over a complete cycle, combined with a structurally low-growth, fragmented, highly cyclical discretionary retail category, an explicitly acknowledged lab-grown-diamond pricing risk to mined-diamond economics, and larger-scale competitors (Pandora, Prouds, Signet, Lovisa) mean the long-term moat remains modest even after a strong turnaround year
